sections.content_markdown: (_ ) I left the fishing rod and the cycle standing against a wall in the courtyard, ready to go the moment I would finish typing the letters.

Look at the sentences below. They do not fit into one paragraph. They refer to two different topics. Separate the sentences for two different paragraphs and rearrange them into two logically connected paragraphs.

* My first day in the new school was difficult.
* There were some benches and an outdoor oven in the picnic area.
* In the National Park of Shalna we found perfect setting for our picnic.
* I got stuck in the traffic jam and reached school fifteen minutes late.
* Everyone had gone to class and I found no one to ask for direction.
* Nearby we found a football field, and not further away, a big pond where some of my friends went swimming immediately.
* Twice I was embarrassed when I walked into classroom that was not mine.
* Behind the picnic area was a forest where some of us went for a walk after lunch.
* The building was so huge that it was hard to find my classroom.
* Finally, I decided to go into my classroom
* When I ultimately got to my class, I was almost in tears.
* We liked the place so much that as we rode home on bus, we agreed to have next year's picnic in the same spot

There are many types of paragraphs. The major types are:

Descriptive paragraph | Narrative paragraph | Cause and Effect paragraph
--- | --- | ---
Comparison paragraph | Contrast paragraph | Expository paragraph
Argumentative paragraph | Persuasive paragraph | Listing paragraph

Some of these types are dealt with elaborately from lesson 3 onward.
